blocking.title: An existing browser spec fails: the playground Angular layout projects still assume the old Angular markup
blocking.evidence: playwright test tests/browser/native-layout-projects.spec.ts: "twelve angular typescript layout projects render and reflow in ar" fails at the section step: expected localName "section", received "hw-section" (browser-subset.log, pw-test-results-subset/). The same test passed before this diff (gate3/v-browser.log, 1.9 minutes). The test stops there; the app-shell step that follows expects one banner and one contentinfo inside the shell, and the playground project projects <strong hwShellHeader> and <small hwShellFooter>, which were given header and footer elements by the component before and sit in div regions now, so it will fail next. pnpm check (build, test, test:browser) therefore fails on this tree. The Angular README has the migration note; the playground projects, the guide samples that use the layout primitives (apps/playground/src/layout-projects.ts, component-layout-guides.ts, component-layout-guides.ar.ts, expanded-samples.ts) and the spec were not migrated. The other 84 tests of the changed areas and the 81 framework example tests pass.
blocking.suggestedFix: Migrate the playground Angular projects and samples to the new markup (<section hwSection label>, a projected header and footer for the shell, the two panes of hw-sidebar) and update the spec, then run the complete browser suite once: this review ran the changed areas only.

major.title: SideNavigation: the current page link fails WCAG 1.4.3 in the default (DGA) theme, light mode
major.evidence: axe color-contrast (serious) on #side a[aria-current="page"] .hw-navigation-drawer-label in all four adapters: 4.31:1, #1b8354 on #f3f4f6, 14px weight 600 (axe-results.json, key nav-en-light). Recomputed from computed styles (harness/contrast-nav.mjs): DGA light 4.32:1, DGA dark 6.43, Hawiyah light 7.03, Hawiyah dark 7.86. The rule is --hw-color-primary-text on --hw-color-surface-muted. It is the NavigationDrawer row rule, so the drawer has the same value; the new component ships with it and is always visible. The proposal premise check already lists "primary-text 4.32" on surface-muted. The token contrast test pairs primary-text with primary-subtle only.
major.suggestedFix: Give the current row a pair that reaches 4.5:1 in every theme and mode (for example the primary-text on primary-subtle pair the token test already covers, or --hw-color-text with the coloured marker), add the pair actually used to packages/tokens/test/contrast.test.mjs, and add an axe run of SideNavigation and NavigationDrawer in DGA light to the browser specs.

major.title: Code listings: Arabic strings on one line change places when highlighted
major.evidence: styles-bidi-arabic-strings.png: const options = ['فاتح', 'داكن']; is drawn with داكن first, and "مرحبا"; // تعليق is drawn with the comment before the string. Measured with Range rectangles of the Arabic letters (harness/bidi.mjs): first string left of second = false; string left of comment = false. With [class*="hw-code-token-"] { unicode-bidi: isolate } both become true. The pre is direction: ltr and unicode-bidi: isolate, but the token spans are not isolated, so the neutral characters between two Arabic runs join the right-to-left run. The proposal names Arabic string literals in code as the case this item exists for.
major.suggestedFix: Add unicode-bidi: isolate to the syntax role rule (it stays at zero specificity), state in docs/code-and-prose.md that a line with more than one Arabic run needs the role spans or bdi, and add a browser assertion for the order of two Arabic string tokens.

major.title: Angular hw-section and [hwSection]: a bound aria-label or role on the host is removed
major.evidence: <hw-section [attr.aria-label]="'Bound name'"> renders <hw-section role=null aria-label=null>, while aria-label="Static name" is kept (harness/section.mjs; scenes-results.json angular.angularExtra.secBound). The host binding [attr.aria-label]="label || authoredLabel" runs after the template binding and writes null; HostAttributeToken reads static attributes only. The same holds for [attr.role] and for <section hwSection [attr.aria-label]>. A localised application binds its names (examples/angular/src/nic-reference.ts:8 does exactly this on a plain section), so moving that markup to the new attribute selector silently drops the accessible name. The tests cover static attributes only.
major.suggestedFix: Do not own aria-label and role through host bindings: write them with Renderer2 when label is set and remove only what the component wrote, or keep the bindings and document that the name must come through the label input, with a development warning when the host also carries an aria-label binding. Add a test with bound attributes.

major.title: Integration is not done and the catalogue count is stated two ways
major.evidence: CONTRACT.md and EXPANSION.md say 85 entries; components.json holds 83 records and says "83 entries", README.md, llms.txt and docs/coverage.md say 83, and the three adapter READMEs still say 77. Neither CopyButton nor SideNavigation appears in components.json, llms.txt, README.md, README.ar.md, docs/coverage.md, the examples or the playground. CHANGELOG.md has no entry for the Angular layout markup change, the hw-portal-actions rename, the group that now opens in NavigationDrawer, or the removed public method HwNavigationDrawerComponent.groupEntries. The builders record all of this as left to an integration phase; AGENTS.md asks for behaviour, styles, APIs, examples and guidance to stay synchronised.
major.suggestedFix: Run the integration phase before this is committed as finished: two catalogue records with evidence, the count in every document, the changelog entry with the migration notes, and usage in the examples or the guide.

minor.title: NavigationDrawer: the close decision is taken in a microtask, which a real click reaches before listeners on ancestors
minor.evidence: links-results.json: with a document listener that only calls preventDefault and no bindLinkNavigation, a trusted pointer click on a drawer link closes the drawer in all four adapters (drawerPreventedTrusted: open=false); the same click made with element.click() leaves it open (drawerPreventedSynthetic: open=true). During a user click the microtask runs when the component listener returns, before the event reaches document. The test nd-closes-after-routed-click asserts "stays open" with a synthetic click only. The routed case itself is right in both forms (drawerRouted: navigate called once, drawer closed, focus back on the trigger). The timing is older than this milestone; the new check and its test rest on it.
minor.suggestedFix: Decide after the dispatch has finished (a zero-delay timer, or a one-time bubble listener on the window) instead of queueMicrotask, and drive the test with a dispatched trusted-like sequence in the browser specs.

minor.title: CopyButton: a repeated immediate failure empties and refills the status inside one task
minor.evidence: copy-results.json: for "empty", "unavailable" and a rejection that settles at once, the mutation sequence is idle, failed, idle, failed, but no animation frame ever sees the empty status (emptyRepeatFrames and the frames arrays hold two entries, not four). With a write that takes time (repeat test) the empty state is rendered. Whether a screen reader repeats an identical message that was cleared and written again before the accessibility tree is updated was not tested with assistive technology.
minor.suggestedFix: Let the result wait for at least one task or frame after the status was emptied when the write settled immediately, or record in the READMEs that only a result that takes time is certain to be announced again. Check with a screen reader.

minor.title: Prose: a class-less pre scrolls without a tab stop, role or name
minor.evidence: axe scrollable-region-focusable on #bare-pre in ar and en, light and dark (styles-results.json axe). The repository spec excludes this rule by name ("apart from the documented class-less listing"). Chromium makes scroll containers focusable by itself; other engines do not all do so.
minor.suggestedFix: Either wrap class-less listings in prose by default (white-space: pre-wrap), so nothing scrolls, or keep the limit and make the Markdown pipeline of the guide add tabindex, role and a name; the guide axe gate should not need the exclusion.

minor.title: Vanilla: the drawer cannot follow a moved current page, and authored markup cannot show the current group open without marking it expanded
minor.evidence: createSideNavigation has refresh(); createNavigationDrawer applies followCurrentGroups once and its controller has no refresh, so after aria-current moves the drawer keeps the old group state (nav-results.json vanilla.drawer: forms=false after the current page moved to it, true in the other three). An authored open attribute counts as expanded, so a server template that opens the group of the current page keeps it open after refresh(); React, Vue and Angular server renders carry open for the current group.
minor.suggestedFix: Recompute the groups when the drawer is shown (or expose refresh() on the drawer controller), and let authors mark an expanded group with a data attribute so that a prerendered open attribute for the current page is not read as expanded.

minor.title: Vue CopyButton: the server render writes an empty style attribute on the root
minor.evidence: renderToString gives <span class="hw-copy" style="" data-state="idle">; the client render and the specification markup have no style attribute (harness/ssr-rv.mjs output; copy-results.json vue.domIcon).
minor.suggestedFix: Pass style only when the application gave one (spread it conditionally).

minor.title: ToggleGroup in React and Vue: a missing label gives an empty legend and no Hawiyah warning (older than this milestone)
minor.evidence: scenes-results.json toggleMissing: React and Vue render <legend class="hw-label hw-sr-only"></legend> and log no "Hawiyah:" warning; Angular omits the legend and warns once. With labelHidden the empty legend is invisible, so the group has no name and nothing reports it. The specification keeps this "unchanged per adapter"; the text contract says a missing required text renders nothing and warns.
minor.suggestedFix: Route the label through text() and needText() in React and Vue and omit the legend when it is missing, as Angular does (milestone 3 parity work if not here).

minor.title: One physical property in the new sticky rule
minor.evidence: overflow-y: auto in .hw-side-navigation[data-sticky="true"]. Every other new rule (code.css, prose.css, copy.css, the header actions) is logical; the same property is used in six older files.
minor.suggestedFix: Use overflow-block: auto here, or record overflow-x and overflow-y as accepted in the stylesheet conventions.

minor.title: Not verified in this review
minor.evidence: No screen reader was used (announcements, the focusable pre with role group). No engine other than Chromium. No Angular CLI ahead-of-time build of a consumer that uses hw-copy-button or hw-side-navigation (the JIT compiler linked the partial declarations in the browser and on the server, and check:packages passed its Angular package format check). React and Vue hydration of the new components rests on the passing unit suites; I rendered both on the server twice and compared the markup, but hydrated only Angular in the browser. The complete browser suite (616 tests, about 40 minutes) was not run: the three new specs, twelve specs of the changed areas and the framework example suite were (206 tests, one failure, B1).

parityDifferences.difference: The host element hw-copy-button is the root (class hw-copy, data-state); React, Vue and vanilla use span.hw-copy. String inputs written as attributes stay on the host (display="text", size, variant, feedbackduration, disabled="").
Server render adds style="" on the root span.

Texts and the value come from options or data-hw-* attributes; variant, size, display and disabled are authored; a bubbling hw:change event follows onCopyResult. Messages are read at each state change.

None in markup inside the root, accessibility tree, tab order, Enter and Space activation, focus, states, icons, status text, results, timed reset, latest-wins, destroy while pending, or missing-text behaviour (copy-results.json).

Root is hw-side-navigation with role="navigation" (or nav[hwSideNavigation] without a role); label is the only source of the name, where React and Vue also accept aria-label or aria-labelledby from the application.
Disabled rows receive tabindex="-1" from the controller (others render a plain span); the current group is opened by the controller, not by the authored markup; refresh() instead of re-rendering.
Not typed with WithNativeAttributes (CopyButton is), so native attributes are untyped in strict templates although they reach the nav.
The list markup is identical in the four adapters and between the two components for the same items; same groups open, same tab order, same reveal (nav-results-all.json, nav-results-angular.json).
Groups follow the current page at creation only.

labelHidden gives legend.hw-label.hw-sr-only as first child with the same name in all four (vanilla: authored). Older differences remain: React adds hw-choice and hw-radio classes and a hidden input, Angular wraps option text in a span, Vue writes data-hw-filled; a missing label is handled differently (m6).

Keeps div.hw-portal-header-main around brand, toggle, navigation and actions; props are navigation and brandHref where Vue and Angular use links and homeHref, and the brand is a link to "/" by default only in Vue, Angular and the authored vanilla markup.
parityDifferences.status: wrapper as specified; names and default older

parityDifferences.difference: The notice and actions containers are always rendered and hidden by :empty when nothing is projected; React, Vue and vanilla render them only with content.
Keeps div.hw-app-shell-body (display: contents) around sidebar and main; Vue and Angular place the four regions directly in the shell.
The three projected regions are always rendered and hidden when empty.
Class order is application class first, then hw-stack; React and Angular write hw-stack first.
A bound aria-label or role on the host is removed.
